newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-DE SILVA HITS HIGHEST TEST SCORE AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DE SILVA HITS HIGHEST TEST SCORE AT HOME.

text.p: Sri Lanka vice-captain Aravinda de Silva reached his highest test score on home soil as the first test against Pakistan headed for a draw on Wednesday.
At tea on the final, de Silva had moved to 166 not out carrying Sri Lanka to 386 for five -- an overall lead of 338.
With only 30 overs remaining to be bowled in the final session, and a declaration not forthcoming from Sri Lankan captain Arjuna Ranatunga, the game has been condemned to a draw.
De Silva passed 150 for the third time in his career, punishing fast bowler Mohammad Zahid. He smacked the second new ball for 16 runs in the bowler's 11th over, including three consecutive fours.
De Silva reached 150 in 432 minutes off 333 balls, striking one six and 13 fours.
His previous highest score at home in a test was 148 against India in 1993-94.

Sri Lanka lost only the wicket of Romesh Kaluwitharana in the middle session for the addition 104 runs. Kaluwitharana, attempting to glance Shahid Nazir, was caught down the leg side by wicketkeeper Moin Khan for 17.

Sanath Jayasuriya, batting down the order due to illness, was at his aggressive best pulling Saqlain Mushtaq over mid-wicket for six as well as hitting five fours to remain unbeaten on 40 at the interval.
